transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love—my workshop, church, even fishing don’t mean anything to me right now. My wife and my pastor finally convinced me to come in because I've just completely withdrawn from everything.
Have you ever had a similar period of depression or loss of interest like this before, or is this the first time it has happened?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before. This is completely new to me, and it's the first time in my life I've ever felt this way.
In addition to losing interest, have you been feeling sad, down, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes, for about the last three weeks, I've felt this heavy, hollow ache in my chest, like someone turned the color down on everything. I just keep wondering what the point of any of this is now, especially with the fear that I might be fading away upstairs.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Sometimes, especially at night when the house is quiet, I find myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn't wake up one morning so my wife wouldn't have to watch me fall apart. I don't have any active plans or intent to actually hurt myself, though. It's just a weary thought that keeps coming back to me.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, such as waking up early, sleeping too much, or not sleeping well, during these past three weeks?
No, I haven't really noticed any major changes or problems with my sleep. It seems to be pretty much the same as it always has been, even with everything else going on.
Have these feelings of low mood and loss of interest been present most of the time for at least two years, or is this episode only the recent three weeks you mentioned?

No, this is definitely a recent change, just over the last three weeks or so. It started quite suddenly after my doctor raised concerns about my memory and told me to cut back on driving, which really hit me hard. I've just felt completely defeated since then.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite or weight over the past three weeks, such as eating much less or losing weight without trying?

Yes, my appetite has dropped off quite a bit lately. I'll often go most of the day on just a cup of coffee and a piece of toast because food just doesn't appeal to me anymore. It feels like way too much effort to even try and fix a proper meal.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating, making decisions, or feeling slowed down in your thinking or movements during these past three weeks?

Yes, both my mind and body feel incredibly slowed down over these last three weeks. I constantly lose my train of thought and struggle with simple decisions like choosing a shirt, feeling like my head is in a foggy blur. My wife has also noticed me shuffling around the house very slowly and sometimes just staring blankly for minutes at a time.

During these past three weeks, have you heard or seen things that other people do not, or felt that you were being watched, blamed, or that your memory problems meant you were losing your mind in a way that others could not understand?

No, I haven't seen or heard anything unusual, and I don't feel like I'm being watched or blamed. I do worry a lot about "losing my mind" because of my memory slips, but it's just a fear of fading away, not anything strange like hearing voices.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself more actively, or made any plans to end your life?

No, I don't have any active plans or thoughts of actually hurting myself. It's really just that feeling of wishing I wouldn't wake up so my wife doesn't have to watch me decline. I would never take any steps to end my own life.

Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, talked more than normal, or did risky things that were out of character for you?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I have never had periods where I felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or acted out of character.

Over the past three weeks, have you had any marked changes in your energy or ability to do daily activities, such as feeling exhausted most of the day or moving and speaking much more slowly than usual?

Yes, over these last three weeks I've slowed down to a crawl, and my wife constantly has to wait on me because I take forever to get dressed or just shuffle slowly around the house. It's incredibly frustrating because I've gone from running our household projects and mentoring kids to barely being able to manage basic chores, relying on her for almost everything now.

During this episode, have you ever felt that you were hearing voices, seeing things others could not, or had strong beliefs that others were trying to harm you or that you were already dead or had no organs?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, and I certainly don't have any of those strange thoughts about people trying to harm me or being dead.
During these past three weeks, have you felt guilty, worthless, or like you are a burden to your family most of the time?

Yes, I feel completely worthless and like a massive burden to my wife. It is incredibly painful to rely so heavily on her for basic things now that I can't think straight or do my usual projects. I often think she would be much better off if I just didn't wake up, so she wouldn't have to watch me fall apart like this.
Have you been feeling depressed or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes, I have felt this way almost every day for the last three weeks, starting right after my doctor brought up the memory testing. I constantly carry a heavy, hollow ache in my chest, and when I look at my tools or fishing rods, I feel absolutely no excitement or curiosity at all.
Have you had any recent medical problems, new medications, or changes in alcohol or substance use that could be contributing to these symptoms?

Yes, my primary care doctor recently raised concerns about possible mild cognitive impairment and ordered neurocognitive testing, which has been a massive source of stress for me. I haven't started any new medications, though, and there haven't been any changes to my alcohol or substance use.
Before these last three weeks, had you already been having ongoing memory or thinking problems for months or years, or did those concerns start only around the same time as this low mood?

The memory and attention lapses, like misplacing my tools and leaving the stove on, actually started first, about six months into my retirement. It was only after my doctor raised concerns about mild cognitive impairment and told me to cut back on driving that this severe low mood and withdrawal took hold over the last three weeks.

Before these memory problems started, had you ever had any head injury, stroke, seizure, or other neurologic illness? Also, do you have any known medical conditions like thyroid disease, vitamin B12 deficiency, or Parkinson’s disease?

No, as far as I know, I don't have any history of head injuries, strokes, or seizures. I've also never been diagnosed with thyroid issues, a B12 deficiency, Parkinson's, or any other neurological conditions.
Have you had any recent head injury, stroke, seizure, new medical illness, or started any new medications around the time your memory problems and low mood began?

No, I haven't experienced any head injuries, strokes, or seizures, and I haven't started any new medications. The only medical concern that has been raised recently is the potential mild cognitive impairment my doctor mentioned.

Have you ever had any similar episodes of low mood or loss of interest before, or is this the first time? Also, during this period, have you noticed changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or feelings of guilt/worthlessness?

Yes, this is the very first time I've ever experienced anything like this, and it all started right after the doctor brought up those memory concerns. Since then, my appetite has plummeted to just coffee and toast because eating feels like too much effort, my concentration is in a constant foggy blur, and I feel completely useless and like a heavy burden to my wife.

Have you noticed any other new medical or neurologic symptoms around the time your memory problems started, such as headaches, weakness, tremor, balance problems, changes in speech, or changes in vision?

No, I haven't experienced any of those specific neurological symptoms. I haven't had any headaches, weakness, tremors, balance issues, or changes in my speech or vision. Everything on that front has been completely normal.

Before these mood symptoms started, were you already having memory or thinking problems that were getting worse, or did the memory issues only begin after you became depressed? Also, has any doctor told you that you have a medical or brain condition that could explain these symptoms?

Yes, the memory lapses like misplacing tools and leaving the stove on started first, about six months into my retirement. It was only after my doctor raised concerns about possible "mild cognitive impairment" and ordered testing three weeks ago that my mood plummeted and I withdrew from everything.

Have you ever had a brain injury, stroke, seizure, or another medical/neurologic illness that could explain the memory problems or the mood changes? Also, have you started any new medications or had any major medical changes around the time these symptoms began?

No, I haven't had any brain injuries, strokes, or seizures, and I haven't started any new medications. The only thing is that my primary care doctor recently raised concerns about possible mild cognitive impairment and ordered neurocognitive testing because of my recent forgetfulness and lapses in attention.
Have you had any recent changes in your memory or thinking that started before the low mood, or any medical/neurologic condition that could explain these symptoms?

Yes, about six months after I retired, I started noticing lapses in my attention and memory, like misplacing my tools and leaving the stove on. My doctor then raised concerns about mild cognitive impairment and ordered testing, which is what triggered this deep depression three weeks ago because I'm so terrified of losing my mind.
Did the low mood and loss of interest begin only after you started noticing memory problems, or were the depression symptoms already present before the cognitive changes?

Yes, the memory problems definitely started first, about six months after I retired. The low mood and loss of interest only took hold over the last three weeks, right after my doctor warned me about cognitive impairment and told me to cut back on driving and my independent activities.

Have your memory or thinking problems been steadily getting worse over time, or do they seem to come and go depending on your mood? Also, have you had any medical tests or been told about a brain or other medical condition that could explain them?

The forgetfulness started gradually about six months into my retirement, but over the last three weeks since my mood declined, it has felt like a constant, frustrating fog. My primary care doctor raised concerns about possible mild cognitive impairment, ordered neurocognitive testing, and advised me to limit driving and other activities while we wait for the results.

Before the last three weeks, did you feel depressed or lose interest in things first, or did the memory and thinking problems start first and then the low mood followed? Also, do the memory problems still happen even when your mood is better?

The memory and thinking problems definitely started first, about six months into my retirement when I was misplacing tools and losing my train of thought. The low mood and heavy feeling only set in about three weeks ago, right after the doctor raised concerns about cognitive impairment and told me to cut back on driving. Since my mood has been consistently low these past three weeks, I haven't really had 'better' days to see if the memory issues improve, though they were certainly there before the depression hit.

Have you been told that your memory problems are due to a specific medical or brain condition, or have you had any tests showing a stroke, dementia, thyroid problem, vitamin deficiency, or other illness that could explain both the memory changes and your depression?

No, I don't have a definitive diagnosis like a stroke or dementia yet; my doctor only mentioned "possible mild cognitive impairment" and ordered neurocognitive testing. It is really the agonizing uncertainty of waiting for those results, combined with being told to cut back on my driving and activities, that triggered this downward spiral and made me feel so useless.

Have you ever been diagnosed with a brain or medical condition, or had any test results showing something like a stroke, dementia, thyroid problem, or vitamin deficiency that could explain both the memory changes and the depression?

No, I haven't been diagnosed with any other medical conditions like a stroke, thyroid problems, or vitamin deficiencies. My doctor did raise concerns about possible mild cognitive impairment and ordered neurocognitive testing, but we don't have those final results yet.

Have you ever been told you have a specific brain or medical condition, or had any test results showing something like a stroke, dementia, thyroid problem, or vitamin deficiency that could explain both the memory changes and the depression?

No, I haven't been diagnosed with any of those things like a stroke, dementia, thyroid issues, or vitamin deficiencies. My doctor ordered neurocognitive testing for possible mild cognitive impairment, but we don't have the final results back yet. It is really the fear of "losing my mind" and the agonizing frustration of waiting for answers that triggered this sudden downward spiral.
